A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UAE-3D/UDM-3D research. All 22 pages of v3 and 23 pages of v4, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original molecular-generation experiments on QM9 and GEOM-Drugs, conditional-generation results, reconstruction measurements, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V4 retains these original results and adds further comparisons and ablations, including encoder-depth and unified-versus-separated latent-space experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed encoder, decoder, reconstruction losses, SE(3) augmentations, DiT diffusion model, and classifier-free guidance remain unchanged. The additional architectures are experimental comparators or ablation controls, not revisions to the proposed pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate unconditional generation on QM9 and GEOM-Drugs and conditional generation for the same six QM9 properties. Newly discussed language, protein, and transcriptomics applications remain future work.

E2.justification: V4 adds SemlaFlow to the QM9 comparison in Table 2 and PerceiverIO to the backbone comparison in Table 4. EQGAT-diff is newly named in the setup paragraph but already appears in v3's benchmark tables.

E3.justification: New ablation protocols vary encoder depth across 3, 6, 9, and 12 layers and compare unified encoding with two separate encoders whose half-width latents are concatenated. Table 7 additionally evaluates reconstruction accuracy and RMSD. Existing benchmark splits and default training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 substantially expands diagnostic testing of the central architecture: Table 10 directly tests unified versus separated latents, Table 8 tests encoder depth, Table 4 adds PerceiverIO, and Table 7 adds reconstruction measurements to the dimensionality analysis. Earlier augmentation, loss-weight, ring-distribution, and latent-visualization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for these experiments. V4 continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V4 adds comparator and diagnostic results while retaining existing UDM-3D benchmark, efficiency, and reconstruction scores. For example, new Table 10 reports 2D FCD of 0.351 for separated latents versus 0.130 for unified latents. Table 2 replaces ADiT's 3D molecule-stability value of 0.000 with an omission; this is not a changed performance estimate.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, diffusion expressions, and guidance derivation in Equations 1–15 are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction and Figure 1 caption qualify previously 'lossless' reconstruction language as 'near-lossless.' The principal claims about unified molecular representations, generation quality, and computational efficiency otherwise retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: V4 adds interpretations concerning coherent distribution learning with unified latents, the sufficiency of six encoder layers, and robustness across diffusion backbones. It also makes the ADiT discussion more qualified about evaluation-protocol differences. The scope and molecule-size limitations are moved, not newly introduced.

D1.justification: V4 adds a code-release statement and repository link in the abstract and specifies the separate-encoder control's inputs, latent widths, and concatenation procedure. Its ADiT discussion adds a tentative account of RDKit/xyz2mol bond inference. The existing hyperparameter table is retained unchanged as Table 13.

R1.justification: V4 adds ten references, including SemlaFlow, PerceiverIO, xyz2mol, and works supporting expanded molecular-language and biological-modeling future directions. The substantive positioning against GeoLDM, ADiT, and MolCRAFT largely remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 moves limitations from Appendix A to the main text, incorporates the earlier language-model future-work paragraph into the conclusion, and reletters the remaining appendices. It adds acknowledgements, updates the conference header, and makes localized prose revisions without broadly restructuring the narrative.

P2.justification: V4 adds Tables 8 and 10 and expands Tables 2, 4, and 7 with comparator rows or columns and reconstruction columns. Existing appendix tables are retained and renumbered. Figure artwork is unchanged, with limited caption edits, relocation, and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The direct unified-versus-separated comparison in v4 Table 10 supplies evidence missing from v3 for the central design choice. Additional architecture checks, more cautious ADiT reporting, and code-access information also improve assessment and reproducibility. These gains are incremental, and new Tables 7–8 report RMSD near 0.002 without reconciling it with the retained 0.0002 Å result in Table 11, limiting the added reconstruction evidence.
